quests.hint: Justify equipment requests with the work problem it solves. Managers say yes to solutions, not preferences.
quests.explanation: A request tied to a work problem ('large spreadsheets') is easier to approve than 'I would like a second monitor'. Explaining the benefit makes it a business need.
quests.situationText: You spend most of the day comparing large spreadsheets on a single small laptop screen. You'd like a second monitor and you're speaking to your manager.
quests.sampleAnswer: Could I get a second monitor? I work with large spreadsheets, and it's hard to manage on one screen.
quests.correctAnswer: Could I get a second monitor? I'm working with large spreadsheets, and it's hard on one screen.
acceptedSynonyms: Could I get a second monitor? I'm working with large spreadsheets, and it's hard on one screen.
Would it be possible to have a second screen? Comparing big spreadsheets on one is quite difficult.
I'd like to ask for a second monitor. It would make my spreadsheet work much easier.
Is it possible to get a second monitor? I'm struggling with large spreadsheets on a single screen.

quests.hint: For urgent IT requests, explain the deadline that makes it urgent. Support teams prioritize by time pressure.
quests.explanation: IT teams get many requests, so the deadline ('a client call in half an hour') tells them why yours is urgent. The word 'locked out' identifies the problem precisely.
quests.situationText: You can't log in to your account and you have a client call in thirty minutes. You've phoned the IT helpdesk.
quests.sampleAnswer: Hello, I'm locked out of my account. Could you reset my password? I've got a client call in half an hour.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm locked out of my account. Could you reset my password, please? I have a client call in half an hour.
acceptedSynonyms: My account is locked, and I have an important call in thirty minutes. Could you help me get back in?
I can't log in, and I have a client call very soon. Is it possible to reset my password quickly?
I'm locked out of my account. Could you reset my password, please? I have a client call in half an hour.
Sorry to rush you, but I'm locked out and need to be online for a client call in half an hour.

quests.hint: Ask for development support by explaining how it improves your work.
quests.explanation: Training requests are accepted when they clearly benefit your job. 'It would help with my reporting' links your interest to a result the company values.
quests.situationText: There's an Excel course next month, and you often struggle to create the reports your team needs. You go to your manager.
quests.sampleAnswer: Would it be possible for me to go to the Excel course next month? It would help with my reporting.
quests.correctAnswer: Would it be possible to attend the Excel training next month? It would help with my reporting.
acceptedSynonyms: Would it be possible to attend the Excel training next month? It would help with my reporting.
Could I sign up for the Excel training next month? I think it would improve my reports.
I'd like to attend the Excel course next month if that's possible. It would make my reporting easier.
Is there any chance I could go on the Excel training? It would really help with my reports.

quests.hint: Start with 'What if we…?' to present an idea as an option, not a criticism. Add the benefit.
quests.explanation: 'What if we…?' invites discussion without attacking the current method. Naming the benefit is important: an idea without a reason is easy to ignore.
quests.situationText: Your team calls each client by phone to remind them about appointments, which takes hours each week. You think an email would be faster.
quests.sampleAnswer: I have an idea. What if we sent the reminders by email instead of calling everyone? It would save a lot of time.
quests.correctAnswer: I have an idea. What if we sent the reminders by email instead of calling everyone?
acceptedSynonyms: Would it make sense to email the reminders? Calling each client takes hours.
How about sending appointment reminders by email instead of phoning people?
I have an idea. What if we sent the reminders by email instead of calling everyone?
Have we thought about using email for the reminders? It could save us a lot of time.

quests.hint: Base your suggestion on an observation you and others share. It makes the idea harder to reject.
quests.explanation: Beginning with 'seems' and a shared observation makes the suggestion collaborative. Phrasing it as a test ('worth trying') feels low-risk to the group.
quests.situationText: Weekly team meetings last an hour, and you notice people lose focus and start checking their phones after about half an hour.
quests.sampleAnswer: Would it be worth trying shorter meetings? It seems like many of us lose focus after half an hour.
quests.correctAnswer: Would it be worth trying a shorter meeting? Half of us seem to lose focus after thirty minutes.
acceptedSynonyms: Would it be worth trying a shorter meeting? Half of us seem to lose focus after thirty minutes.
Could we try cutting the meeting to thirty minutes? People seem to switch off after that.
I wonder if a shorter meeting might work better. Attention seems to drop after half an hour.
How about testing a half-hour meeting? I think we lose focus later on.

quests.hint: Point out the inefficiency with facts, then suggest one clear fix. Ask, don't demand.
quests.explanation: 'I've noticed' introduces an observation politely, and a single clear solution makes it actionable. Ending with a question lets your manager decide.
quests.situationText: You realize the team enters the same customer data into two systems each week. You'd like to propose one shared sheet to your manager.
quests.sampleAnswer: I've noticed we enter the same data twice. Could we use one shared sheet instead?
quests.correctAnswer: I've noticed that we enter the same data in two places. Could we use one shared spreadsheet instead?
acceptedSynonyms: We seem to be doing the same data entry twice. Would a single shared sheet work better?
I've realized that we type the same information into two systems. Could we combine them?
I've noticed that we enter the same data in two places. Could we use one shared spreadsheet instead?
Something I've noticed is the duplicate data entry. Might it be possible to use one shared file?

quests.hint: Agree with a person by name, then add your own point. 'I'd just add' makes your contribution sound complementary.
quests.explanation: Referring to a colleague's idea by name gives credit and builds alliances. 'I'd just add' shows you agree while offering something new.
quests.situationText: In a meeting, Sam suggests launching the app in March. You agree, but you know that testing usually takes longer than planned.
quests.sampleAnswer: I think Sam's right. The only thing I'd add is that testing may take longer.
quests.correctAnswer: I agree with Sam. I'd just add that we'll need more time for testing.
acceptedSynonyms: I think Sam's right. The only thing I'd add is that testing may take longer.
I'm with Sam on this, but we should allow additional time for testing.
That makes sense to me, Sam. We'll just need to plan for more testing.
I agree with Sam. I'd just add that we'll need more time for testing.

quests.hint: Disagree by acknowledging the point, then naming your concern with a reason. Don't say 'you're wrong'.
quests.explanation: 'I see your point, but…' protects the relationship while you disagree. Focusing on 'my concern' rather than 'your mistake' keeps the debate about the problem, not the person.
quests.situationText: A colleague proposes finishing the whole project in four weeks. You believe the budget doesn't cover the extra staff this would require.
quests.sampleAnswer: I see your point, but I'm concerned that's too tight for our budget.
quests.correctAnswer: I see your point, but I'm worried that timeline is too tight for our budget.
acceptedSynonyms: I understand the reasoning, but I'm not sure our budget allows for that.
I see your point, but I'm worried that timeline is too tight for our budget.
That's a fair suggestion, but I'm concerned the budget won't cover it.
I can see why you'd want that, but I think it would put too much pressure on our budget.

quests.hint: Separate what you agree with from what you don't. Partial agreement is realistic and respectful.
quests.explanation: Saying 'I partly agree' shows you've evaluated the whole proposal. Separating the strong points from the doubtful one makes your criticism specific and constructive.
quests.situationText: A manager presents a new product plan. You like the design but doubt the launch date is realistic.
quests.sampleAnswer: I partly agree. The design is strong, but I'm not sure the launch date is realistic.
quests.correctAnswer: I partly agree. The design is strong, but I don't think the launch date is realistic.
acceptedSynonyms: I agree with much of it. The design is excellent, but I have doubts about the launch date.
There's a lot I like, especially the design. My concern is whether the launch date can be met.
The design convinces me, but I'm not so sure about the timing of the launch.
I partly agree. The design is strong, but I don't think the launch date is realistic.

quests.hint: Take shared responsibility for the misunderstanding, then state what you understood. 'We might have' avoids blame.
quests.explanation: 'We might have misunderstood each other' shares the responsibility, so nobody loses face. Stating what you thought gives the other person the chance to correct it.
quests.situationText: Your colleague expects the report this Friday, but you've planned to finish it next Friday. You realize this when she asks for it.
quests.sampleAnswer: Sorry, there seems to have been a mix-up. I understood the deadline as next Friday.
quests.correctAnswer: I think we might have misunderstood each other. I thought you meant next Friday, not this one.
acceptedSynonyms: Sorry, there seems to have been a mix-up. I understood the deadline as next Friday.
I think we had different ideas. I was working towards next Friday.
I think we might have misunderstood each other. I thought you meant next Friday, not this one.
We may have crossed wires. I thought the report was due next Friday.

quests.hint: Correct a misread message by clarifying what you meant, not what they got wrong.
quests.explanation: 'That's not quite what I meant' is gentler than 'You misunderstood'. Restating your original intention ('the cost, not the timing') clarifies the point without arguing.
quests.situationText: You emailed a colleague asking about the project. She replied about the deadline, but you were asking about the cost.
quests.sampleAnswer: I should have been clearer. What I need to know is the cost, not the time.
quests.correctAnswer: Sorry, that's not quite what I meant. I was asking about the cost, not the timing.
acceptedSynonyms: Sorry, that's not quite what I meant. I was asking about the cost, not the timing.
I think my question wasn't clear. I was asking about the cost, not the deadline.
Thanks, but I actually meant the cost. Sorry, my email wasn't clear.
I should have been clearer. What I need to know is the cost, not the time.

quests.hint: If you're unsure about who is responsible, check without assuming. Frame it as your own confusion.
quests.explanation: Asking 'Was that meant to be me?' takes the blame away from anyone and helps to solve unclear responsibilities. It avoids a bigger problem later, such as a missed client call.
quests.situationText: You believed your colleague Sam would call an important client, but the client says nobody has called. You speak to your manager.
quests.sampleAnswer: There seems to be some confusion about the client call. Who was meant to make it?
quests.correctAnswer: I thought Sam was handling the client call. Was that supposed to be me?
acceptedSynonyms: I assumed Sam was calling the client. Did you want me to do it?
Sorry, I understood that Sam would call the client. Was I supposed to?
I thought Sam was handling the client call. Was that supposed to be me?
There seems to be some confusion about the client call. Who was meant to make it?

quests.hint: Answer with company, your name, and an offer. It's the professional pattern in nearly every workplace.
quests.explanation: The standard call-opening sequence identifies the company, the speaker, and offers help. This gives the caller everything they need without asking questions.
quests.situationText: You work at the front desk of a company called Bright Solutions, and the phone rings at nine o'clock in the morning. Your name is Maya.
quests.sampleAnswer: Hello, this is Maya at Bright Solutions. How can I help?
quests.correctAnswer: Good morning, Bright Solutions. Maya speaking. How can I help you?
acceptedSynonyms: Hello, this is Maya at Bright Solutions. How can I help?
Bright Solutions, good morning. Maya speaking. What can I do for you?
Good morning, you've reached Bright Solutions. This is Maya. How may I assist you?
Good morning, Bright Solutions. Maya speaking. How can I help you?

quests.hint: When transferring a call, say where you're sending the caller and warn about the wait.
quests.explanation: Explaining a transfer prevents the caller from thinking they've been disconnected. Saying 'one moment' signals a short delay.
quests.situationText: A caller asks about buying a bulk order, which the sales team deals with. You need to transfer him.
quests.sampleAnswer: That would be handled by our sales team. Let me put you through. One moment, please.
quests.correctAnswer: Let me put you through to the sales department. One moment, please.
acceptedSynonyms: I'll transfer you to sales, who can help with that. Please hold for a moment.
Let me put you through to the sales department. One moment, please.
For a bulk order, you'll need sales. I'll connect you now, if you don't mind holding.
Our sales department can help you with that. Let me transfer your call.

quests.hint: If you don't know an answer, say so honestly and promise a specific follow-up. It's better than guessing.
quests.explanation: Being honest about not knowing, then promising a time for a reply, builds trust. 'I'll find out' and 'this afternoon' turn a limit into a commitment.
quests.situationText: A customer asks about the warranty period on a product, and you don't know it. You need to check with the technical department.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'm afraid I don't have that information right now. I'll find out and call you back this afternoon.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm afraid I don't have that information to hand. I'll find out and call you back this afternoon.
acceptedSynonyms: I don't know the answer at the moment, but I'll check and phone you back this afternoon.
Sorry, I can't say for sure. Let me look into it and get back to you this afternoon.
I'll need to check that with our technical team. May I call you back this afternoon?
I'm afraid I don't have that information to hand. I'll find out and call you back this afternoon.

quests.hint: Name the item and the day. 'Did you get it?' is neutral, while 'You didn't reply' would sound like an accusation.
quests.explanation: Giving the day and item makes the person's search easier. A simple question 'Did you get it?' is polite and neutral, while 'You didn't reply' would sound accusing.
quests.situationText: You emailed an invoice to a client on Monday. It's now Thursday and you haven't heard back. You meet the client by chance in the corridor.
quests.sampleAnswer: Just checking that you received the invoice I emailed on Monday.
quests.correctAnswer: I sent you the invoice on Monday. Did you get it?
acceptedSynonyms: Just checking that you received the invoice I emailed on Monday.
I sent you the invoice on Monday. Did you get it?
I emailed the invoice on Monday. Has it arrived on your side?
Did the invoice I sent on Monday come through okay?

quests.hint: A follow-up on an unanswered request should be friendly and specific. Ask whether they've had time, and don't demand.
quests.explanation: 'Have you had a chance to look at it?' assumes the person is busy, not careless. It reminds them about the request while leaving room for their situation.
quests.situationText: A week ago, you sent a colleague in another department a request for approval. You haven't heard back and you'd like a response.
quests.sampleAnswer: Could I ask about the request I sent last week? I'd be grateful for an update.
quests.correctAnswer: I wanted to check on the request I sent last week. Have you had a chance to look at it?
acceptedSynonyms: Just following up on my request from last week. Do you know when you might be able to look at it?
I'm getting in touch about the request I sent you last week. Have you had a chance to review it?
Could I ask about the request I sent last week? I'd be grateful for an update.
I wanted to check on the request I sent last week. Have you had a chance to look at it?

quests.hint: Confirm receipt, thank the sender, and say what happens next. It tells them the ball is in your court.
quests.explanation: Confirming receipt with a next step ('I'll review them today') gives the sender peace of mind and shows reliability.
quests.situationText: A supplier has just sent you five files you were waiting for. You reply over the phone to say you have them.
quests.sampleAnswer: Thanks for sending the files. I've received them, and I'll review them today.
quests.correctAnswer: Thank you for sending the files. They've arrived, and I'll go through them today.
acceptedSynonyms: I've got the files, thanks. I'll take a look this afternoon and let you know.
Thank you for sending the files. They've arrived, and I'll go through them today.
The files came through, thank you. I'll review them today.
Received, thanks. I'll check the documents today and get back to you.

quests.hint: Ask for a single day off with a direct, polite question. Give the date so no time is wasted.
quests.explanation: For a single day off, a short polite request is enough. Stating the date and asking 'Would that be okay?' leaves the decision with your manager.
quests.situationText: You want to take next Friday off for a personal matter. You speak to your manager at the start of the week.
quests.sampleAnswer: Would you mind if I took next Friday off?
quests.correctAnswer: I'd like to take Friday off. Would that be okay?
acceptedSynonyms: I'd like to take Friday off. Would that be okay?
Would it be possible for me to be off next Friday?
I wanted to ask if I could take next Friday as a day off.
Would you mind if I took next Friday off?

quests.hint: For longer leave, show you have planned for your absence. It makes approval easier.
quests.explanation: A week off requires more consideration from a manager. Promising to finish your project first shows you're thinking about the team, not only yourself.
quests.situationText: You'd like to take the last week of August for a family holiday. You have an important project due in mid-August.
quests.sampleAnswer: Could I take the last week of August off? I'll finish my project before I go.
quests.correctAnswer: Could I take the last week of August off? I'll have my project finished before I leave.
acceptedSynonyms: I'd like to request leave for the last week of August. My project will be done by then.
Would it be possible to book the last week of August as holiday? I'll complete my project first.
Could I take the last week of August off? I'll have my project finished before I leave.
I'm hoping to be away the last week of August. I'll make sure my project is done before I go.

quests.hint: If you need to leave during the day, give the time and the reason, and offer to make up the time.
quests.explanation: Leaving early is a small request, so keep it short. A brief reason and an offer ('I'll make up the time') keep the tone respectful.
quests.situationText: You have a doctor's appointment at four o'clock and you'd need to leave at three. You find your manager before lunch.
quests.sampleAnswer: Would it be all right if I left an hour early today? I have a doctor's appointment.
quests.correctAnswer: Would it be all right if I left an hour early today? I have a doctor's appointment, and I can make up the time.
acceptedSynonyms: Would it be all right if I left an hour early today? I have a doctor's appointment, and I can make up the time.
Is it okay if I leave at three today? I have a medical appointment.
May I go an hour early today? I've got an appointment with the doctor.
I need to leave early today for a doctor's appointment. Would that be fine?

quests.hint: Enter a meeting late by acknowledging it briefly and not interrupting more than needed.
quests.explanation: A short apology and 'please carry on' show respect without disrupting the meeting. It's better than a long explanation that draws attention to you.
quests.situationText: You're ten minutes late for a team meeting because of a previous call. Everyone is already discussing the agenda as you enter the room.
quests.sampleAnswer: Sorry, I got held up on a call. Don't stop, I'll catch up as I go.
quests.correctAnswer: Sorry I'm late, everyone. Please carry on. I'll catch up.
acceptedSynonyms: Apologies for being late. Don't stop on my account.
I'm sorry to come in late. Please continue, and I'll follow along.
Sorry I'm late, everyone. Please carry on. I'll catch up.
Sorry, everyone. My last call ran over. Please go on.

quests.hint: To ask a colleague to be quieter, focus on your need, not on their behavior. Suggest another option.
quests.explanation: Requests for quiet are more successful when they describe your situation ('I'm trying to finish a report') and offer a solution ('the meeting room'). It avoids saying the person is being rude.
quests.situationText: A coworker is speaking loudly on the phone at his desk next to yours, and you have a deadline for a report in one hour.
quests.sampleAnswer: Excuse me, I'm on a tight deadline. Could you take your call somewhere quieter?
quests.correctAnswer: Sorry to bother you, but I'm trying to finish a report. Would you mind taking that call in the meeting room?
acceptedSynonyms: Sorry to bother you, but I'm trying to finish a report. Would you mind taking that call in the meeting room?
Excuse me, I'm on a tight deadline. Could you take your call somewhere quieter?
I hate to interrupt, but I'm trying to concentrate on a report. Could you move to the meeting room for the call?
Sorry, would it be possible to take that call in another room? I need to focus on a deadline.

quests.hint: Claim your belongings lightly. A gentle joke or an assumption of a mistake keeps things friendly.
quests.explanation: Assuming an honest mistake ('I think that might be mine') avoids accusing the person of stealing. Mentioning a name label gives evidence without confrontation.
quests.situationText: In the office fridge, you see a coworker about to take a sandwich with your name on the wrapper, thinking it's the one she brought.
quests.sampleAnswer: Oh, I think that sandwich might be mine. My name's on the wrapper.
quests.correctAnswer: Excuse me, I think that sandwich might be mine. It has my name on it.
acceptedSynonyms: Sorry, I think you've picked up mine by mistake. It has my name on it.
Ah, that one's actually mine. See, my name's on the wrapper.
Excuse me, I think that sandwich might be mine. It has my name on it.
I think that's my lunch. There's a label with my name on it.

quests.hint: For 'Tell me about yourself', give your job, your experience, and one strength. Keep it under thirty seconds.
quests.explanation: Interviewers use this question to see how you organize your thoughts. A concise structure (role, experience, strength) shows clarity and focuses on what matters for the job.
quests.situationText: In a job interview, the interviewer smiles and says, 'So, tell me a little about yourself.' You're a graphic designer. You have five years of experience and enjoy working in small teams.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'm a graphic designer with five years' experience, and I enjoy working closely with small teams.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm a graphic designer with five years of experience. I enjoy working with small teams.
acceptedSynonyms: I work as a graphic designer, and I've been doing it for five years. I like working in small, close teams.
I'm a designer with five years of experience in graphics, and I'm at my best in small teams.
I've spent five years as a graphic designer, and what I enjoy most is teamwork in small groups.
I'm a graphic designer with five years of experience. I enjoy working with small teams.

quests.hint: 'I need a job' is a weak answer. Link your own goals to something the company offers.
quests.explanation: A strong answer connects your growth to what the employer offers. It shows you have researched the company and aren't just applying anywhere.
quests.situationText: The interviewer asks why you applied for this role. You want to work on bigger projects, and you admire the company's reputation.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'm interested in this role because I want to work on bigger projects, and your company has a great reputation.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm interested in this role because I'd like to work on bigger projects, and your company has an excellent reputation.
acceptedSynonyms: I applied because I want to grow into larger projects, and your company is well respected.
I'm interested in this role because I'd like to work on bigger projects, and your company has an excellent reputation.
This role appeals to me as a chance to handle bigger projects, and I admire your company's reputation.
I'd like to take on bigger challenges, and your company has a strong name in the industry.

quests.hint: When the interviewer invites your questions, ask about the real job. It shows serious interest.
quests.explanation: A question about a typical day shows you're thinking about doing the job well. It's much more useful than asking about holidays too early.
quests.situationText: At the end of the interview, the interviewer asks, 'Do you have any questions for us?' You'd like to know more about the daily work.
quests.sampleAnswer: Yes, I do. Could you tell me what a typical day in this role would look like?
quests.correctAnswer: Could you tell me what a typical day in this role looks like?
acceptedSynonyms: I'd like to know what a normal day is like in this position.
What would my daily responsibilities be in this role?
Could you describe a typical day for someone in this job?
Could you tell me what a typical day in this role looks like?

quests.hint: A good status report covers what's done, what's in progress, and what blocks you. Link them in order.
quests.explanation: Listing done, in progress, and blocked tells your manager exactly where the project stands, and it highlights what you need from others. It's a summary structure you can use every week.
quests.situationText: It's Friday afternoon and your manager asks for a quick status update on your project before the weekend. You're waiting for figures from your colleague Sam.
quests.sampleAnswer: The report is finished, the presentation is about half done, and I'm waiting for Sam's figures before I can complete it.
quests.correctAnswer: I've finished the report and I'm halfway through the presentation, but I need Sam's figures to complete it.
acceptedSynonyms: I've finished the report and I'm halfway through the presentation, but I need Sam's figures to complete it.
I've completed the report. The presentation is half finished, and I'm still waiting on Sam's figures.
The report is done, and I'm halfway through the presentation. I can't finish without Sam's figures.
Report done, presentation about half done, and I need figures from Sam to complete it.

quests.hint: Agree to help, but set clear limits. A precise offer is better than a vague yes.
quests.explanation: Saying what you can and can't do avoids problems later. Stating your limit ('I'm out on Wednesday') isn't refusing; it's protecting both of you from false expectations.
quests.situationText: A colleague going on holiday asks if you can answer her customer calls while she's away this week. You can help on Monday and Tuesday only.
quests.sampleAnswer: Sure, I can take your calls on Monday and Tuesday, but I'm not in on Wednesday.
quests.correctAnswer: I can cover your calls on Monday and Tuesday, but I'm out on Wednesday.
acceptedSynonyms: Happy to help on Monday and Tuesday, but I won't be here on Wednesday.
I can answer your calls for the first two days, but not on Wednesday. I'm away then.
I can cover your calls on Monday and Tuesday, but I'm out on Wednesday.
I'm able to cover Monday and Tuesday. Wednesday isn't possible for me.

quests.hint: At the end of the week, sign off with a contact instruction. Tell people how to reach you only if it's really needed.
quests.explanation: Ending the day with clear availability prevents confusion. 'If anything urgent comes up' limits interruptions to real emergencies and shows professionalism.
quests.situationText: It's Friday at five and your team is still in the office. You're leaving, but a client issue could arise during the evening.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'm leaving for the weekend. If something urgent happens, please ring my mobile.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm heading off now. If anything urgent comes up, you can call me on my mobile.
acceptedSynonyms: I'm heading off now. If anything urgent comes up, you can call me on my mobile.
I'm leaving for the weekend. If something urgent happens, please ring my mobile.
I'm off now. For anything urgent, you can get me on my mobile.
I'm going home. If there's an emergency, my mobile is on.
